pilots.title: North Dakota Bookkeeping
pilots.description: North Dakota bookkeeping for purchase use tax, ND TAP withholding records, vendor bills and financial reporting.
pilots.summary: Delivery and work locations connect North Dakota tax reporting to the ledger. Keep them attached to the underlying transaction.
pilots.notice: General bookkeeping information. Confirm filing positions with a qualified tax professional using current instructions and your business facts.

sections.heading: North Dakota Sales And Purchase Review
paragraphs: The Office of State Tax Commissioner administers sales and use tax and provides filing access through ND TAP. Preserve sales details, tax charged, delivery addresses and exemption support with the reporting period. Review customer refunds against the original sale so tax adjustments remain traceable.

For accounts payable, connect each vendor invoice to receiving evidence, payment and the location where goods are used. Flag purchases without tax for review rather than automatically treating the vendor invoice as the final tax determination.

sections.heading: Employer Withholding Records
paragraphs: North Dakota employers register for income tax withholding through ND TAP. The official guidance distinguishes residents, work performed in the state and wages paid for work elsewhere. Maintain actual residence and work location changes, withholding authorizations and payroll registers so a payroll specialist can evaluate those facts.

As a general bookkeeping control, reconcile gross wages, deductions and employer costs separately. Match withholding payments with filed reports and leave an explanation for any unpaid balance. A payroll provider withdrawal can contain several components.

sections.heading: Income, Spending And Vendor Evidence
paragraphs: Keep customer invoices and deposits distinct from owner funding and borrowing. A farm supply business, for example, may receive a lender advance and customer payments on the same day; the deposit description should identify the source before posting.

For machinery or equipment, retain the purchase agreement, delivery charges, financing terms and any trade documentation. Present uncertain capitalization and personal use questions to the preparer with the original evidence.
sections.source_context: General bookkeeping reference. The example and monthly routine are practical illustrations, not additional state requirements.

sections.heading: Monthly Financial Reporting
paragraphs: Reconcile operating cash, credit cards and equipment debt before producing a profit and loss statement and balance sheet. Review seasonal customer balances and unpaid supplier bills with the owner. Identify deposits in transit and bills received after the close instead of burying them in miscellaneous expense.

Maintain a separate purchase tax review schedule with vendor, date, use location, amount, decision and return reference. Its unresolved items should appear in the monthly discussion even when the bank balance reconciles.
sections.source_context: General bookkeeping reference. The example and monthly routine are practical illustrations, not additional state requirements.

sections.heading: Hypothetical Equipment Delivery
paragraphs: Hypothetical example: a North Dakota repair shop receives a diagnostic unit from another state and sees no tax on the invoice. The bookkeeper attaches delivery evidence, records the equipment separately from repair parts and asks the preparer to resolve use tax. The example assumes no exemption, rate or automatic liability.

sections.heading: Unemployment Reports And Owner Income
paragraphs: Job Service North Dakota uses UI EASY for quarterly Contribution and Wage Reports, electronic payment and account management. The system calculates total, excess and taxable wages and issues a submission confirmation. Keep that confirmation with a payroll wage bridge; reconcile the calculated contribution to employer unemployment expense, the liability and the eventual bank payment.

North Dakota's S corporation and partnership page describes Forms 60 and 58 and state treatment following the relevant federal entity classification. It also addresses nonresident owner withholding. Give the preparer owner residence and ownership changes, income and deduction detail, distributions and state activity evidence. Reconcile any approved owner withholding separately from employee withholding and document whether an owner payment is a distribution or expense.

sections.heading: Year End And Preservation
paragraphs: Give the tax preparer the reconciled ledger, inventory support, equipment documents, loan statements, payroll totals and ND TAP return and payment copies. Include a list of transactions still awaiting tax treatment rather than marking the year complete with unsupported entries.

North Dakota Century Code Section 57 40.2 09 requires covered invoices and other records of tangible personal property bought for resale or use to be preserved for three years and three months. This is a purchase record rule, not a universal disposal date. Maintain separate payroll and property schedules and preserve open audit or disputed filing records.

pilots.title: Ohio Bookkeeping
pilots.description: Ohio bookkeeping for sales and purchase tax, Commercial Activity Tax receipts, withholding and monthly close records.
pilots.summary: Ohio gross receipts reporting can require a different view of activity from the profit and loss statement. Build that bridge alongside sales and payroll schedules.
pilots.notice: General bookkeeping information. Confirm filing positions with a qualified tax professional using current instructions and your business facts.

sections.heading: Sales And Purchase Tax Evidence
paragraphs: Ohio sales tax covers tangible personal property and selected services; use tax addresses taxable purchases where sales tax was not collected. Keep the taxable sales detail, exemption support and transaction location with each reporting period.

Save the location evidence and tax calculation used in the sales system. For vendor purchases, retain invoices and receipt locations and flag untaxed supplies or equipment for use tax review. Ohio's use tax statute includes exceptions where the applicable sales tax was paid and requires support for claimed exemptions.

sections.heading: Commercial Activity Tax Receipts
paragraphs: Ohio's CAT statute imposes a gross receipts privilege tax on the business rather than directly on its customers. It distinguishes prohibited invoicing of the tax from recovery through prices and specified written lease arrangements. Determine applicability with the preparer using the current year rules, then keep a receipts schedule that can be reconciled to the ledger.

Do not assume net profit is the CAT reporting base. Separate sales proceeds, returns, financing deposits and other receipts, and provide transaction support for the preparer's inclusion and sourcing decisions. Avoid turning a monthly expense report into an unsupported gross receipts return.

sections.heading: Payroll And School District Evidence
paragraphs: Ohio employer guidance addresses both employer and school district withholding and electronic filing and payment. Retain completed IT 4 forms, employee residence and school district information, compensation dates, gross wages and tax withheld.

Reconcile each withholding liability to payroll registers, filed reconciliations and remittances. Route an employee move to the payroll specialist before changing the residence field alone; keep the effective date and the authorization supporting the revised setup.

sections.heading: Payables And Monthly Statements
paragraphs: As general accounting practice, connect supplier bills to delivery and approval records and record credits against the original purchase. Separate resale stock, operating supplies and fixed assets so purchase tax review can use meaningful categories.

At close, reconcile banks, cards, receivables and payables and issue a profit and loss statement and balance sheet. Present the CAT receipts bridge with sales tax and payroll liability rollforwards so the owner can see why tax reporting totals differ from revenue or cash deposits.
sections.source_context: General bookkeeping reference. The example and monthly routine are practical illustrations, not additional state requirements.

sections.heading: Hypothetical Ohio Distributor
paragraphs: Hypothetical example: a distributor records a customer sale, a bank loan and an owner contribution in one month. The bookkeeper labels the three receipts and supplies the sales documents to the CAT preparer. Adding all deposits or using net profit would leave the preparer without the required transaction analysis.

sections.heading: Unemployment Contributions And Quarterly Wages
paragraphs: Ohio law requires contributory employers to file quarterly contribution and wage reports showing total and taxable remuneration, individual wages and weeks paid. Its administrative rule calls for prescribed electronic transmission and continued reporting until written permission to discontinue. Keep the employer account and assigned rate notice with the payroll file, separately from Ohio income tax withholding.

Treat the report and contribution payment as separate evidence. Reconcile reported wages, taxable wages and the assigned contribution calculation to unemployment expense and the closing liability, then carry unpaid contributions visibly into cash planning. Include these reports with the CAT receipts bridge in the year end handoff. A cash shortage does not remove the quarterly report requirement.

sections.heading: Year End Records And Retention
paragraphs: Assemble the final receipts bridge, sales and use returns, payroll reconciliation, asset purchases, debt statements and open questions for the tax preparer. Include the current CAT applicability conclusion rather than copying a prior year threshold.

Ohio's CAT record rule generally requires four years from the return due date or filing date, whichever is later, with written authority for earlier destruction or longer retention. The 2026 employer filing instructions require accurate withholding records for at least four years from the due date. These distinct periods are not a universal authorization to destroy sales, asset or disputed records.

pilots.title: Oklahoma Bookkeeping
pilots.description: Oklahoma bookkeeping for delivery sourcing, purchase use tax, cash rounding records, payroll and vendor documentation.
pilots.summary: Oklahoma transaction detail needs to preserve delivery location and tax before a cash rounding adjustment. Those fields also make month end reconciliation more reliable.
pilots.notice: General bookkeeping information. Confirm filing positions with a qualified tax professional using current instructions and your business facts.

sections.heading: Sales Location And Cash Receipts
paragraphs: Oklahoma Tax Commission guidance distinguishes a sale at the seller's business from goods delivered to the purchaser elsewhere. Keep the customer receipt location and sales tax calculation with the invoice, especially when deliveries cross municipal or county lines.

The Commission says sales tax continues to be calculated to the nearest cent before cash rounding, with the exact tax shown on the receipt remitted. If the business rounds cash change, use a distinct adjustment account so rounding cannot alter recorded tax collected.

sections.heading: Vendor Purchases And Use Tax
paragraphs: Oklahoma use tax can apply to property brought into the state for storage, use or consumption, with applicable local use tax. Link vendor bills to the delivery location, purpose and evidence of tax already charged. Send untaxed business equipment and supplies for review.

Use separate purchase categories for resale inventory, tools and office consumption. Attach credit memos and returns to the original bill; a later supplier refund should not erase the evidence that explains the original purchase.

sections.heading: Employer Withholding
paragraphs: The state describes withholding as employee tax collected by the employer and paid to the state, with OkTAP used for returns and payments. Keep payroll registers, worker authorizations, gross wages, deductions and payment confirmations.

Reconcile liability accounts to filed reports rather than posting the whole payroll withdrawal as wages. Obtain current withholding instructions and verify the assigned payment schedule with the payroll specialist. This page supplies no wage rate or deposit deadline.

sections.heading: Financial Close And Income Evidence
paragraphs: As general accounting practice, tie sales system totals to card settlements and cash counted, showing refunds, processing charges and cash rounding separately. Reconcile bank and credit card statements and investigate negative customer or vendor balances.

Prepare the profit and loss statement and balance sheet with a short schedule of purchase tax questions and unpaid payroll liabilities. Separate owner contributions and loan proceeds from customer income and preserve the agreements supporting those cash inflows.
sections.source_context: General bookkeeping reference. The example and monthly routine are practical illustrations, not additional state requirements.

sections.heading: Hypothetical Cash Counter Sale
paragraphs: Hypothetical example: an Oklahoma shop chooses to round a cash customer's change while its card sales remain exact. The bookkeeper retains the receipt's tax calculation and posts only the cash difference to rounding. A delivery invoice is reviewed separately using its purchaser receipt location.

sections.heading: OESC Wages And Entity Income
paragraphs: OESC requires quarterly wage reports on active accounts, including quarters without wages or taxable wages. Reports identify employee name, Social Security number and gross wage and support unemployment tax and benefit calculations. Keep the filed wage listing, contribution calculation and payment together and reconcile employer unemployment expense separately from employee state withholding.

Oklahoma's corporate guidance distinguishes income allocated to resident S corporation shareholders from nonresident shares lacking the specified shareholder agreement. Preserve owner residence, allocations, agreements and distributions for the preparer. Keep estimated entity payments and any approved owner related liability in identifiable accounts so the year end income handoff can reconcile federal results to the Oklahoma filing without guessing from cash transfers.

sections.heading: Year End Handoff And Record Preservation
paragraphs: Provide the preparer with reconciled revenue, rounding totals, vendor purchase review, payroll reports, asset invoices and filed OkTAP records. Oklahoma publishes current withholding tables and local rate resources; archive the version used when a transaction or payroll setting changes.

Oklahoma's sales and use rules describe a three year books and records preservation period and require written Commission authorization for earlier destruction under the specified conditions. Keep the source documents and electronic data needed to verify tax. Confirm separate payroll periods and preserve asset or disputed return support longer when needed.

pilots.description: Oregon bookkeeping for transit payroll distinctions, supplier documentation, income records and monthly financial reporting.
pilots.summary: Oregon has no general sales tax, while payroll reporting can contain several separate state programs. Preserve enough detail to explain each liability.
pilots.notice: General bookkeeping information. Confirm filing positions with a qualified tax professional using current instructions and your business facts.

sections.heading: Sales And Supplier Documentation
paragraphs: Oregon's Secretary of State explains that Oregon has no sales tax while other state and local taxes apply. Preserve sales by customer location and activity so the preparer can evaluate taxes outside the general sales tax system and obligations in other states.

For accounts payable, retain vendor bills, shipment destinations and tax charged by another state. A supplier charge is not automatically refundable because the purchaser is based in Oregon. Keep inventory, equipment and operating purchases separate and send uncertain treatment to the preparer.

sections.heading: Two Different Transit Payroll Concepts
paragraphs: Oregon's Statewide Transit Tax is imposed on employee wages and the employer withholds, reports and remits it. The agency explicitly distinguishes that program from Lane and TriMet transit payroll taxes, which are imposed on employers. Give each applicable program its own ledger liability.

Preserve employee residence, actual work locations, wages and payroll deductions. Maintain the evidence used to decide whether district payroll tax applies. A single generic transit tax account can conceal whether an amount was withheld from workers or charged to the employer.

sections.heading: Combined Reporting And Payroll Close
paragraphs: The withholding and payroll page describes combined reporting through Frances Online, including withholding, unemployment, transit programs, Workers' Benefit Fund and Paid Leave Oregon contributions. Save the filed report and the payment breakdown by program.

As a general control, compare the payroll register to gross wage expense, employee deductions and employer charges. Reconcile each remittance with the correct agency period and retain annual reconciliation support. Do not infer that a payroll service bank debit proves every component was filed.

sections.heading: Income And Monthly Financial Statements
paragraphs: Identify customer revenue separately from customer advances, financing and owner transfers. For a project business, maintain an invoice schedule that connects work completed, billed amounts and collections on the agreed accounting basis.

Close bank and card reconciliations and review inventory, unpaid bills and payroll clearing. Present a profit and loss statement, balance sheet and cash commitments. Explain any difference between payroll expense and payments caused by liabilities recorded in one month and remitted in the next.
sections.source_context: General bookkeeping reference. The example and monthly routine are practical illustrations, not additional state requirements.

sections.heading: Hypothetical Oregon Design Studio
paragraphs: Hypothetical example: a studio adds a worker whose duties occur at several locations. The bookkeeper documents those locations and supplies them to the payroll specialist, who evaluates the applicable district programs. The Statewide Transit Tax withholding remains separately tracked instead of being merged into employer transit expense.

sections.heading: Commercial Activity And Unemployment Expense
paragraphs: Oregon's CAT is additional to corporate income tax and applies through its own commercial activity framework. DOR distinguishes commercial receipts, excluded items and a qualifying expense subtraction. Keep a bridge from accounting revenue to reviewed Oregon activity, supported by customer destinations and exclusion documents. Preserve cost inputs and labor detail separately so the preparer can evaluate the subtraction rather than deducting all ledger expenses.

Oregon Employment Department requires quarterly Form OQ reporting and sends employer billing statements reflecting the account balance. Match those statements to unemployment expense, reported contributions, payments and the closing payable. Keep employee wage detail and each program calculation with Form OQ and respond to Frances information requests. Provide this reconciliation alongside the CAT receipts and expense bridge; neither schedule substitutes for the other.

sections.heading: Year End And Retention Decisions
paragraphs: Send the preparer reconciled payroll program balances, annual reporting support, sales by location, supplier invoices, asset purchases and ownership or loan transactions. Identify any unreviewed district assignment or other state sale.

The 2026 combined payroll instructions require WBF assessment records for at least four years and other covered payroll records for at least six years after required reports are filed. Apply those tax reporting periods to the relevant records while reviewing other personnel and asset requirements separately. Export filed reports and underlying payroll detail before changing providers.

pilots.description: Pennsylvania bookkeeping for purchase tax evidence, separate business records, withholding and financial close.
pilots.summary: Pennsylvania record rules require usable transaction evidence, including why a purchase was treated as nontaxable. A payment alone cannot answer that question.
pilots.notice: General bookkeeping information. Confirm filing positions with a qualified tax professional using current instructions and your business facts.

sections.heading: Sales And Purchase Records
paragraphs: Pennsylvania requires businesses to report use tax on taxable purchases when the seller has not collected the tax. Keep invoices and evidence of tax paid, or document the reason a purchase was considered nontaxable. Record the nature, use, price and relevant dates.

The recordkeeping regulation calls for daily and reporting period sales detail by outlet, including cash and credit sales. It also addresses separate books for distinct retail and other business activities. Organize these records before summarizing them in the general ledger.

sections.heading: Employer Evidence
paragraphs: Pennsylvania withholding guidance considers both employee residence and where services occur, including reciprocal arrangements supported by the appropriate certificate. Keep work locations, employee declarations and the effective dates of changes with the payroll record.

As a general control, compare compensation and tax withheld in payroll registers with filed reports and payments. Give local payroll obligations their own review task; a state withholding reconciliation does not resolve every municipality or work location question.

sections.heading: Payables, Income And Expense
paragraphs: Match a supplier bill to the receiving record and its payment. A retailer that also installs products should retain the contract and job reference so inventory purchases, installation costs and business assets can be traced to the correct activity.

Separate credit sales from collections in the customer ledger. Identify owner transfers, borrowing and refunds before recording bank deposits as income. Keep explanations for disputed bills and customer credits.
sections.source_context: General bookkeeping reference. The example and monthly routine are practical illustrations, not additional state requirements.

sections.heading: Monthly Statements And Tax Reconciliation
paragraphs: General bookkeeping practice is to reconcile banks, cards, customer balances and unpaid bills before issuing a profit and loss statement and balance sheet. Compare outlet sales totals with ledger revenue and explain timing differences in card settlements.

Include a purchase use tax schedule with invoice references and the preparer's decisions. Tie reported tax and payments to ledger liabilities, leaving adjustments visible so the next month's opening balance has a clear explanation.
sections.source_context: General bookkeeping reference. The example and monthly routine are practical illustrations, not additional state requirements.

sections.heading: Hypothetical Two Activity Business
paragraphs: Hypothetical example: a Pennsylvania business sells cabinets at retail and performs construction work. The bookkeeper uses separate activity codes and attaches purchase purpose and job details, giving the preparer evidence to evaluate each transaction rather than applying the retail treatment to every job.

sections.heading: UCMS Reporting And Entity Tax Handoff
paragraphs: Pennsylvania's UCMS process requires covered employers to file quarterly wage and tax reports and remit contributions. The wage reporting page distinguishes gross and taxable wages, employee wage detail and credit weeks, and provides correction reports. Retain those components and compare them with payroll records. Accrue employer contributions distinctly, explain wage basis differences and match payments to the covered quarter.

Pennsylvania recognizes federal S status unless the business elects otherwise for Pennsylvania; its guidance describes owner shares of income, loss and credit. Give the preparer the election file, ownership history, resident and nonresident owner detail and state adjustments to income and expenses. Preserve distributions and capital activity separately from deductible spending and keep state entity tax payments traceable to the approved filing.

sections.heading: Year End And Retention
paragraphs: Supply reconciled outlet sales, purchase review, payroll reports, asset invoices, loans and unresolved classifications to the tax preparer. Include filing acknowledgments and an account of every material year end adjustment.

Section 34.2 requires its sales and use tax records to remain available for at least three years from the end of the calendar year to which they relate. Preserve longer when another applicable rule or an open matter requires it; that period does not establish a disposal date for all payroll and asset records.

pilots.description: Rhode Island bookkeeping for electronic sales detail, TDI deductions, vendor purchases and monthly reporting.
pilots.summary: Rhode Island electronic record requirements make a readable transaction export valuable. Payroll also needs to distinguish employee TDI deductions from employer costs.
pilots.notice: General bookkeeping information. Confirm filing positions with a qualified tax professional using current instructions and your business facts.

sections.heading: Sales Detail And Electronic Records
paragraphs: Rhode Island sales tax applies to retail sales, rentals or leases of many goods and services. Preserve the item sold, selling price, tax due, invoice number, sale date and payment method. The record regulation also calls for POS terminal and transaction identifiers.

The regulation addresses procedures for electronic systems and access to the records themselves. Keep a written description of who maintains the system and how records are checked. A monthly bank total does not preserve the item detail needed to explain taxable and exempt sales.

sections.heading: Vendor Bills And Purchase Review
paragraphs: Rhode Island's rule includes purchase totals for resale and for use or consumption. Connect the vendor invoice to the item received, intended use and tax charged. Preserve source documents and return workpapers alongside the ledger.

For general accounts payable control, retain purchase approvals, returns and credit memos. Review untaxed equipment and supplies with the preparer. Do not mix an inventory resale purchase with goods taken from stock for business use.

sections.heading: Withholding And TDI
paragraphs: State income tax withholding is separate from TDI deductions. The Department of Labor and Training explains that employees fund TDI through payroll deductions while employers handle collection and remittance. Its Employer Tax Unit processes quarterly wage and tax reports containing the applicable programs.

Keep employee deductions separate from employer Employment Security and Job Development costs. Reconcile gross pay, each liability and remittances to the wage report. Save correction explanations when a payroll provider revises wages.

sections.heading: Income And Monthly Financial Reports
paragraphs: As general practice, record gross customer sales, refunds and processor charges before matching the bank settlement. Reconcile cash drawers to sales detail and explain overages or shortages using a distinct account.

After bank, card, customer and vendor reconciliations, issue a profit and loss statement and balance sheet. Include a payroll liability summary that lets the owner distinguish money withheld from employees from company payroll expense.
sections.source_context: General bookkeeping reference. The example and monthly routine are practical illustrations, not additional state requirements.

sections.heading: Hypothetical POS Change
paragraphs: Hypothetical example: a Rhode Island shop changes payment systems. Before access ends, the bookkeeper exports individual sales with item, tax and transaction identifiers, saves the return workpapers and documents where the export is stored. A settlement PDF alone would leave missing sales evidence.

sections.heading: Corporate Income And Employer Tax Reconciliation
paragraphs: Rhode Island Corporate Tax starts from federal taxable income and uses state additions, deductions and sales apportionment. The agency also identifies minimum taxes and charges involving S corporations and other entity types. Maintain federal to state adjustment workpapers, sales destination support, ownership changes and entity classifications for the preparer. A low profit month does not itself settle an annual minimum obligation.

The Employer Tax Unit identifies Employment Security contributions as employer funded and processes Form TX-17 along with the other applicable programs. Build a quarterly wage bridge from payroll to the filed report, then reconcile each employer contribution and employee TDI deduction to its ledger liability and payment. Send the approved rates, filed reports and any open benefit charge correspondence with the year end records.

sections.heading: Year End And Retention
paragraphs: Prepare the tax handoff with reconciled sales detail, vendor purchases, payroll wage reports, TDI deduction reconciliation, asset documents and filing copies. Flag missing electronic data while it can still be recovered.

The active Rhode Island record regulation requires covered sales and use records for at least three years unless written authority permits earlier disposal. Confirm separate periods for payroll, property and open disputes before destroying those categories.

pilots.description: South Carolina bookkeeping for separately stated installation charges, wholesale records, withholding and financial statements.
pilots.summary: South Carolina installation treatment depends on both customer billing and reasonable support in the books. Preserve that connection when closing the month.

sections.heading: Installation And Sales Records
paragraphs: SCDOR explains that installation incidental to a retail property sale is excluded from sales and use tax when separately stated and reasonable based on the seller's books and records. Keep the customer invoice and evidence of the installation work together.

The sales and use manual also requires separate wholesale and retail records. Use a sales classification supported by the transaction documents rather than a single untaxed revenue category covering every exclusion.

sections.heading: Purchases And Vendor Documentation
paragraphs: SCDOR's manual identifies purchase invoices bearing vendor names and addresses as part of required records. Add purchase approval, delivery and payment evidence as general accounts payable controls.

Distinguish goods held for sale from installation supplies, equipment and business consumption. Send untaxed purchases and unclear contracts for tax review, keeping the preparer's conclusion attached to the invoice rather than relying on a ledger label alone.

sections.heading: Employer Withholding
paragraphs: Employers with wages earned in South Carolina who are required to file federal withholding returns are also state withholding agents. SCDOR describes withholding, quarterly reporting and payment responsibilities. Maintain employee declarations, work locations, pay registers and remittance evidence.

Compare tax withheld with the payroll liability and filed return, separately from employer payroll expense. Nonresident contractor payments can also raise withholding questions; flag relevant vendor arrangements for a specialist before assuming payroll is the only withholding account.

sections.heading: Monthly Income And Financial Close
paragraphs: As general bookkeeping practice, reconcile the sales system to customer balances and cash settlements, with returns and card fees identified. Reconcile supplier balances to statements and preserve disputed invoices without deleting their history.

Issue a profit and loss statement and balance sheet after bank and card reconciliations. Include an installation revenue and cost review where relevant so the owner can see whether invoice descriptions and supporting job records agree.

sections.heading: Hypothetical Appliance Installation
paragraphs: Hypothetical example: a South Carolina retailer sells an appliance with installation. The bookkeeper saves the separately stated invoice, technician hours and job cost support for the preparer's reasonableness review. Merely moving part of a bundled invoice into an installation ledger account would not supply that evidence.

sections.heading: SUITS And Business Income Records
paragraphs: South Carolina DEW uses SUITS for unemployment wage reports, payments, liability determinations and contribution rate history. Its wage page identifies bonuses, commissions, tips and certain other payments as reportable wages. Reconcile those payments to payroll records and retain the specialist's explanation of exclusions before matching taxable wages and contribution expense to the report.

SCDOR's S corporation page describes SC1120S, an annual license fee and an available annual election for eligible active trade or business income. Keep capital and paid in surplus records, shareholder allocations and the election decision with the tax handoff. Show income tax, license fees and payroll liabilities separately; a shareholder distribution should not silently reduce operating expense or the capital base used by the preparer.

sections.heading: Year End And Retention
paragraphs: Give the preparer the wholesale and retail bridge, installation support, purchase review, payroll totals, asset purchases and filed return copies. Identify exceptions where a customer invoice and internal job record do not agree.

SCDOR's September 2025 sales and use manual states that records must be kept for four years, citing Regulation 117.200.1. Apply that instruction to the covered records and confirm longer preservation for open audits, property support and other record categories.

sections.heading: Job Records And Owner Materials
paragraphs: South Dakota distinguishes qualified utility projects from other construction projects. For nonqualified utility projects, its contractor excise guidance includes owner furnished material in the prime contractor's gross receipts and does not allow a deduction for subcontractor payments.

Keep a job schedule containing owner material values and the date furnished, alongside billed receipts. Preserve project specific prime contractor exemption certificates where applicable. An ordinary cash income report does not capture every element of this tax calculation.

sections.heading: Purchase Tax And Supplier Evidence
paragraphs: The contractor guidance also addresses state and municipal use tax on material where prior sales or use tax payment is undocumented. Obtain supplier invoices or owner evidence of tax paid and connect them to the particular project.

For general payables control, match invoices to delivery tickets and approvals, distinguish materials from tools and equipment, and retain subcontractor agreements and credits. Avoid treating an owner's purchase as adequately documented simply because it never passes through the contractor's bank.

sections.heading: Employer Reemployment Accounts
paragraphs: South Dakota's Department of Labor and Regulation administers Reemployment Assistance. Keep the employer account notices and assigned reporting instructions with payroll records and obtain a specialist determination of applicable coverage.

As a monthly control, reconcile gross wages, employer unemployment costs and payments to wage reporting. Preserve worker locations, time records and explanations for corrected wages. A subcontractor invoice should remain subject to classification review.

sections.heading: Income, Expense And Financial Reporting
paragraphs: Reconcile contract billings, customer advances and collections by job. Report subcontractor costs as costs on the agreed accounting basis while keeping the separate excise reporting schedule intact.

After cash, card, payroll and supplier reconciliations, provide a profit and loss statement and balance sheet. Include job margins and forthcoming cash needs so an excise tax adjustment is not mistaken for an unexplained change in operating revenue.

sections.heading: Hypothetical Owner Supplied Fixtures

sections.heading: Quarterly Reemployment And Income Tax Scope

Review benefit charge statements with the owner because those records concern the employer account rather than employee withholding.

South Dakota DOR states that the state does not impose a corporate income tax, but separately requires bank franchise returns from covered financial institutions. That limited distinction does not remove federal income reporting, tax obligations elsewhere or the sales and contractor taxes discussed here. Give the preparer a complete profit and loss statement, asset basis, debt and owner transactions and identify any financial institution activity requiring specialized review.

sections.heading: Year End And Record Retention

South Dakota DOR states that businesses subject to sales, use or contractor excise tax must keep business records for at least three years, including returns and supporting worksheets. Treat open disputes and other record categories separately before any disposal.

pilots.description: Tennessee bookkeeping for business receipts, entity tax handoffs, sales and purchase tax and employer records.
pilots.summary: Tennessee business tax, sales tax and franchise and excise tax need different supporting schedules. Track the relevant activity without assuming one registration settles all three.
pilots.notice: General bookkeeping information. Confirm filing positions with a qualified tax professional using current instructions and your business facts.

sections.heading: Gross Receipts And Entity Records
paragraphs: Tennessee business tax guidance considers business activity within counties and incorporated municipalities. Keep receipts by business location and activity, with refunds and other adjustments identified, so the preparer can evaluate applicability under current rules.

Franchise and excise tax has a separate entity and activity framework. Preserve formation documents, tax elections, ownership changes and prior filings. A business income report alone cannot establish an entity exemption or determine franchise tax.

sections.heading: Sales, Use Tax And Payables
paragraphs: Tennessee sales tax includes state and local portions. Use tax can apply to otherwise taxable products brought or shipped into the state where sales tax was not collected. Retain sale and purchase descriptions, destination evidence and exemption documentation.

As general accounts payable practice, match supplier bills to purchase approvals, receipts and payments. Separate inventory, equipment and consumption purchases and maintain a review list for invoices without tax. A supplier address outside Tennessee does not establish the final treatment.

sections.heading: Employer Unemployment Records
paragraphs: Tennessee requires employers to complete online registration so unemployment liability can be determined. Keep the registration result, account notices, wage reports and assigned instructions with payroll records.

Reconcile employee gross pay, deductions, employer charges and payroll cash withdrawals separately. Retain actual work locations and classification support. Submit corrected wage facts to the payroll specialist rather than offsetting unexplained differences against current wages.

sections.heading: Monthly Income And Financial Reporting
paragraphs: Use customer invoices to distinguish revenue, advances and collections on the agreed accounting basis. Reconcile borrowing and owner funding separately from operating receipts, and maintain a bridge from ledger revenue to business tax review schedules.

Close bank, card, payroll and supplier reconciliations before presenting the profit and loss statement and balance sheet. Include cash commitments for payroll, vendor bills and tax liabilities so entity tax estimates can be planned without confusing them with sales tax collected.

sections.heading: Hypothetical New Tennessee Location
paragraphs: Hypothetical example: a Tennessee LLC opens a second shop in another municipality. The bookkeeper records the new location's receipts and expenses and provides its opening date to the preparer. The entity file and franchise and excise work remain separate from the business location review.

sections.heading: Employer Contributions And Filing Status
paragraphs: Tennessee's current employer FAQ directs wage reporting and amendments through Employer e-Services, replacing the prior TNPAWS and TPU systems. Preserve the employee wage detail and report summary as well as the successful submission evidence. Compare gross and taxable wages with payroll and accrue employer unemployment premiums separately from net pay and federal payroll deductions.

For the business and franchise and excise schedules already described, maintain a state adjustment file that identifies asset additions, disposals, depreciation differences and owner transactions for the preparer. Tie approved estimated payments and final return balances to distinct liability accounts. When a filing position changes, preserve the preparer's adjustment and its effective year so the owner can understand why cash tax commitments differ from reported accounting profit.

sections.heading: Year End And Retention
paragraphs: Deliver location receipts, entity records, sales returns, vendor review, payroll reports, fixed asset invoices and financing statements with a reconciled ledger. Show any missing returns or unresolved classifications explicitly.

The Department's sales and use manual requires dealer records for a minimum of three years from December 31 of the year the related return was filed. Records tied to an appealed assessment remain until final disposition. Unregistered activity and fraud can involve earlier periods; the rule is not a blanket disposal date.

pilots.notice: General bookkeeping information. Confirm filing positions with a qualified tax professional using current instructions and your business facts.

sections.heading: Sales Tax And Business Cash
paragraphs: Utah Tax Commission describes sales and use tax as trust fund taxes held for the state until remitted. Maintain a liability account for tax collected and reconcile it to sales records, return adjustments and payments.

sections.heading: Vendor Purchases And Expense Support
paragraphs: Utah's recordkeeping page calls for receipts, canceled checks and other evidence supporting income tax deductions or credits, along with sales and exemption records. Match supplier bills to purchase authorization, goods received and payment. Record the purpose and use location of equipment and supplies and submit untaxed purchase questions to the preparer.

Keep resale inventory distinct from goods withdrawn for business use. Preserve equipment invoices and financing terms for asset basis decisions. A bank description identifies cash movement but seldom explains what was purchased or how it was used.

sections.heading: Employer Annual Reconciliation
paragraphs: Utah employer guidance requires annual withholding reconciliation for each year or partial year an account exists, even when there are no employees or withholding to report. The reconciliation is part of the fourth quarter return process.

The agency describes TC-941E and wage or information statement submissions as separate components. Retain submission acknowledgments for each. Reconcile gross wages, Utah income, amounts withheld and remittances before the provider submits annual data.

sections.heading: Monthly Financial Reporting
paragraphs: Close cash, credit card and payroll clearing reconciliations and review open customer and supplier balances. Use a profit and loss statement and balance sheet to show operations and obligations on the agreed accounting basis.

Present sales tax and withholding liability rollforwards separately, with opening balance, new activity, payments and closing balance. Investigate a missing submission confirmation as an unresolved filing matter even if the bank payment cleared.

sections.heading: Hypothetical Quiet Payroll Year
paragraphs: Hypothetical example: a Utah business stops paying employees during the year but keeps its withholding account open. The bookkeeper saves the last payroll and account status and asks the payroll specialist to complete the required annual reconciliation. Zero later payroll does not itself demonstrate completion.

sections.heading: Workforce Contributions And Owner Withholding
paragraphs: Utah Workforce Services requires covered employers to file a quarterly wage list and contribution report online, including zero wage quarters until the account is closed or exempted. Preserve individual gross wages, excess wage calculations and the assigned rate with the submission. Reconcile the employer contribution expense and liability against the report and payment rather than treating it as employee withholding.

Utah's pass through withholding page addresses partnerships, S corporations and LLCs classified as partnerships. Owner residency and type can affect withholding review. Give the preparer owner allocations, residence evidence, distributions and Utah source income detail, and maintain approved owner withholding separately from wages. The Workforce page requires its specified employer records for four calendar years, a distinct period from the general tax assessment framework.

sections.heading: Year End Records And Retention
paragraphs: Provide the preparer with sales detail, purchase review, payroll annual submissions, equipment records, bank reconciliations and owner or loan transactions. Keep the reconciliation evidence and unresolved items with the year end package.

Utah's recordkeeping page directs taxpayers to statutory standards and exceptions. Section 59 1 1406 ties covered books and records to assessment exposure; Section 59 1 1410 generally allows three years after filing, with special deemed filing dates and exceptions for unfiled or fraudulent returns and extensions. Confirm the applicable dates before disposal and preserve property basis and open matters separately. Workforce Services separately requires its specified unemployment reporting records for four calendar years.

sections.heading: Meals, Rooms And Local Activity
paragraphs: Vermont requires businesses selling taxable meals or rooms to collect and remit Meals and Rooms Tax and obtain the relevant license. Keep receipts separated by meals, alcohol, rooms and other activity rather than using one hospitality revenue total.

The agency identifies local option taxes and separately administered city taxes in Burlington and Rutland. Preserve the business and delivery locations needed for a local review. Do not copy a neighboring property's tax setup without checking the actual location.

sections.heading: Service Charges And Payroll Evidence
paragraphs: Vermont's compliance guidance distinguishes voluntary customer tips from charges imposed by the operator and emphasizes the treatment of amounts retained by the operator. Retain the customer bill, stated charge and evidence of distribution to employees for preparer review.

Employer registration instructions also address Vermont income tax withholding on wages for employees working in Vermont. Reconcile tip and service charge distributions to payroll, employee withholding and cash payments so the same receipt is not counted as both owner revenue and employee money without explanation.

sections.heading: Vendor Purchases And Income Records
paragraphs: As general accounting practice, connect ingredient, linen and equipment invoices to receiving records and payment. Keep purchases used in the business distinct from merchandise for resale and flag invoices with uncertain tax treatment.

Reconcile reservation deposits, cancellations, refunds and final charges to guest accounts. Identify loans and owner contributions separately from hospitality income. Keep the original booking evidence when a platform settlement deducts fees.

sections.heading: Monthly Hospitality Financial Reports

Add a service charge reconciliation showing collections, employee distributions, retained amounts and unresolved differences. Present tax liabilities by applicable program with return and payment references. This is general bookkeeping practice for a usable monthly close.

sections.heading: Hypothetical Vermont Event Meal

sections.heading: Employer Quarterly Reports And Entity Returns

pilots.title: West Virginia Bookkeeping
pilots.description: West Virginia bookkeeping for municipal boundaries, purchase use tax, wage withholding and monthly reconciliations.
pilots.summary: West Virginia municipal tax can depend on the actual boundary rather than a familiar postal place name. Keep delivery and use locations visible in the records.
pilots.notice: General bookkeeping information. Confirm filing positions with a qualified tax professional using current instructions and your business facts.

sections.heading: Municipal Sales And Use Locations
paragraphs: West Virginia Tax Division administers municipal sales and use taxes and provides rate and boundary tables. Its guidance warns that even a nine digit postal code need not match a municipality's boundaries. Retain the physical delivery or service location behind the tax assignment.

Municipal use tax can apply to taxable purchases used in a taxing municipality when municipal sales tax was not paid. Record where supplies and equipment are used, not only the supplier's mailing address. Ask the preparer to resolve boundary questions from the transaction facts.

sections.heading: Supplier Bills And Customer Income
paragraphs: Keep the vendor invoice, delivery ticket and evidence of tax paid together. For materials moved between jobs, identify the destination and purpose so the preparer can review municipal purchase tax treatment.

As general accounting practice, match supplier credits to original bills and distinguish resale goods, consumed materials and equipment. Match customer deposits to invoices and identify borrowing and owner transfers separately from revenue.

sections.heading: Employer Withholding
paragraphs: West Virginia describes withholding as employee tax deducted by the employer and remitted to the state. Its guidance includes commissions, bonuses, vacation allowances and tips among compensation categories. Preserve the wage detail needed to explain each component.

Reconcile gross wages and employee withholding with payroll registers, filed returns and payments. Record work location and employee authorization changes with effective dates, and leave worker classification or multistate treatment to the payroll specialist.

sections.heading: Monthly Financial Statements
paragraphs: General monthly close work includes bank and card reconciliations, open receivable review, supplier statement comparison and payroll clearing review. Produce a profit and loss statement and balance sheet using the business's agreed accounting basis.

Maintain municipal tax totals by reporting location alongside state tax totals. Explain liability timing differences and unresolved delivery assignments. A clean bank reconciliation does not demonstrate that each sale was assigned to the correct municipality.
sections.source_context: General bookkeeping reference. The example and monthly routine are practical illustrations, not additional state requirements.

sections.heading: Hypothetical Boundary Delivery
paragraphs: Hypothetical example: a West Virginia supplier delivers identical materials to two sites sharing a postal town name. The bookkeeper preserves each street address and checks the actual municipal assignment before applying the prepared tax setup. The example assumes no rate and no automatic exemption.

sections.heading: WorkForce Contributions And Business Income
paragraphs: WorkForce West Virginia requires a complete quarterly Wage and Contribution Report and provides an online employer system. Keep its account and wage records apart from Tax Division withholding. Reconcile individual wage totals and employer contributions to payroll expense, the contribution payable and payments, while retaining separation and benefit charge correspondence for the responsible reviewer.

The Tax Division describes corporation net income tax and separate or combined unitary reporting. Its pass through page addresses nonresident partner or shareholder withholding and the NRW-4 agreement. Give the preparer entity and ownership records, state activity, owner residency, income and expense adjustments and agreements. Approved owner withholding belongs in its own reconciliation, with distributions and tax payments traced rather than grouped with employee wage costs.

sections.heading: Year End And Preservation
paragraphs: Provide municipal and state schedules, wage reports, purchase documents, asset history and filed return copies with reconciled financial statements. Highlight any supplier invoice missing proof of tax.

Tax Division TSD 450 says records supporting filed returns should remain while returns are subject to audit and describes the ordinary three year period from filing, with early returns generally treated as filed on their due date. Fraud or unfiled returns may reach further. This audit framework does not set one destruction date for payroll, property or disputed records.

pilots.title: Wisconsin Bookkeeping
pilots.description: Wisconsin bookkeeping for mixed business activity, exemption support, payroll accounts and financial records.
pilots.summary: Wisconsin requires separate records when taxable retail operations accompany another nontaxable activity. Design revenue categories that preserve that distinction.
pilots.notice: General bookkeeping information. Confirm filing positions with a qualified tax professional using current instructions and your business facts.

sections.heading: Mixed Activity And Exemption Evidence
paragraphs: Wisconsin DOR says a business combining retail sales and other nontaxable activities must maintain separate records for determining sales and use tax. Without the separation, tax may be imposed on all business receipts.

For exempt sales, its guidance identifies purchaser name and address, sale date, item, exemption amount and reason. Preserve a completed certificate where applicable and connect it to the relevant sales. A generic exempt sales total cannot explain an individual transaction.

sections.heading: Vendor Purchases And Use Tax
paragraphs: DOR directs people with regular use tax obligations from untaxed purchases to obtain the relevant certificate. Keep a review of supplier invoices with item description, use location, tax charged and the preparer's determination.

As general accounts payable practice, match bills to receipt and approval evidence. Separate beginning and ending inventory, operating purchases and assets. Preserve vendor credits and proof of tax paid so refunds or corrections can be evaluated without reconstructing the purchase later.

sections.heading: Employer Account Records
paragraphs: Wisconsin maintains a separate withholding program and publishes wage statement and information return resources. Keep the employer account notices, employee authorizations, wage detail and filing acknowledgments with payroll records.

Reconcile each payroll liability to the register and remittance history. Compare annual wage statement totals to year to date payroll before submission and retain an explanation for corrections. Confirm current filing instructions with the payroll professional.

sections.heading: Monthly Income And Reporting
paragraphs: General close work should reconcile bank and card balances, customer receivables, unpaid bills and payroll clearing. Produce a profit and loss statement and balance sheet with revenue classifications that agree to the taxable and nontaxable activity schedules.

Identify owner transfers, loan proceeds and customer collections separately. Review margins by activity when shared expenses are allocated, retaining the allocation method so a reporting change is explainable to the owner and preparer.
sections.source_context: General bookkeeping reference. The example and monthly routine are practical illustrations, not additional state requirements.

sections.heading: Hypothetical Workshop And Retail Counter
paragraphs: Hypothetical example: a Wisconsin business has a retail counter and a separate service activity believed to be nontaxable. The bookkeeper preserves contracts and distinct sales records and asks the preparer to confirm treatment. Posting all deposits to service revenue would erase the transaction distinction.

sections.heading: DWD Contributions And Entity Elections
paragraphs: Wisconsin unemployment is administered through DWD rather than the DOR withholding account. Its employer handbook requires quarterly reporting even in quarters without payroll. Wage detail accompanies the contribution tax report. Save both reports, the rate notice and payment and reconcile wages, employer unemployment expense and the closing liability. Keep correction support with the quarter affected.

DOR's corporation and partnership resources distinguish tax option S corporation and partnership entity level elections, apportionment and owner withholding resources. Preserve the current election, owner residency and allocations, state income modifications and other state tax payments for the preparer. Match approved entity payments to the correct year and keep distributions and guaranteed payments distinguishable so the financial statements support the chosen reporting framework.

sections.heading: Year End And Record Retention
paragraphs: Supply the activity bridge, exemption file, purchase review, payroll annual support, equipment invoices and debt records with the final reconciled accounts.

Wisconsin DOR says sales and use records must remain for the four year period open to audit, longer where an agreement extends it, and until a contested determination is finally resolved. Its individual income guidance separately identifies longer basis support for property and loss carryforwards. Apply the relevant category rather than discarding everything after four years.

pilots.title: Wyoming Bookkeeping
pilots.description: Wyoming bookkeeping for sales and purchase tax evidence, employer registration, asset records and monthly reporting.
pilots.summary: Wyoming tax records should explain merchandise purchases and business consumption alongside sales. Employer registration also creates records outside the revenue tax account.
pilots.notice: General bookkeeping information. Confirm filing positions with a qualified tax professional using current instructions and your business facts.

sections.heading: Sales And Purchase Documentation
paragraphs: Wyoming law requires sales tax records and invoices supporting merchandise purchased for resale. Its use tax law separately addresses records of goods stored, used or consumed in the state. Retain the item, transaction date, destination and evidence of tax paid.

The Excise Tax Division provides sales and use filing resources and official educational material. Keep the sales return workpapers and source transactions together. For vendor purchases, flag invoices without tax and give the preparer the actual use facts instead of assuming that an online seller's treatment is conclusive.

sections.heading: Payables And Equipment History
paragraphs: As general bookkeeping practice, match each vendor bill to purchase approval, receipt and payment. Keep resale stock, shop consumption and equipment separate so purchases can be reviewed meaningfully.

Maintain an asset worksheet with acquisition date, cost, invoice, serial identifier where useful, financing, business use location and disposal evidence. Preserve trade and sale documents with the original acquisition record for the preparer's basis and tax review.
sections.source_context: General bookkeeping reference. The example and monthly routine are practical illustrations, not additional state requirements.

sections.heading: Employer Registration And Payroll
paragraphs: Wyoming DWS directs employers to complete joint business registration so workers compensation and unemployment coverage can be determined. Its instructions recommend saving the registration summary and supporting questionnaire.

Keep coverage determinations, rate notices, worker classifications and job locations with payroll records. Reconcile wage totals and applicable employer charges to reports and payments, separately from net wages. Registration evidence should remain accessible even when a provider handles payroll.

sections.heading: Monthly Income And Financial Statements
paragraphs: Reconcile customer invoices and collections, identify owner funding and loans and review deposits held for future work. Match inventory movements with sales and purchases rather than treating every stock purchase as an unexplained cash expense.

After bank, card, debt and payroll reconciliations, present a profit and loss statement and balance sheet. Include an asset additions schedule and purchase tax questions so a major equipment outlay is visible in both financial reporting and the preparer's review.
sections.source_context: General bookkeeping reference. The example and monthly routine are practical illustrations, not additional state requirements.

sections.heading: Hypothetical Machine Replacement
paragraphs: Hypothetical example: a Wyoming shop replaces a machine and sells the old unit. The bookkeeper preserves both invoices, financing and delivery evidence and links the disposal to the original asset record. The preparer can review purchase and sale tax treatment without relying on the net cash difference.

sections.heading: WYUI Contributions And Annual Asset Reporting
paragraphs: Wyoming DWS uses WYUI for quarterly unemployment reports and amendments, tax payments and review of wages, rates, credits and benefit charges. Reconcile the report's contribution amount to employer unemployment expense and the payable, then match the payment. Keep workers compensation amounts separately identifiable even where the same employer portal is used.

Wyoming Secretary of State requires registered entities to file annual reports and pay the applicable asset based license tax or flat fee. Its official worksheet calls for assets located and employed in Wyoming and prescribes valuation distinctions for depreciable assets, depletable assets and land. Prepare the location and valuation bridge from the balance sheet with assessment support for the preparer; net equity or the month's profit is not the worksheet's total asset measure.

sections.heading: Year End And Retention
paragraphs: Give the preparer sales and purchase tax schedules, asset worksheets, equipment documents, payroll reports, DWS notices and debt statements with reconciled accounts.

Wyoming sales law Section 39 15 107 requires covered vendor books and resale invoices for three years. Use tax Section 39 16 110 separately requires covered books and purchase invoices for three years. Preserve records for open matters and confirm payroll and asset requirements before applying a disposal date to those categories.
